<!-- pr-reviewer: ed277f7417467fbec0eca8aca4a58b4fdc2bad10 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** (Collision-law change, reviewed at full rigour.)

### What looks good
- One predicate, `is_upright` (`crates/sim/src/verify/upright.rs:29`), with one named constant `UPRIGHT_TILT_RAD = 1e-9` rad (~5.7e-8 deg). The exact `is_vertical` case keeps its exact answer, so the prismatic branch is unchanged bit for bit for already-vertical poses; `camcraft_cl::is_vertical` itself is untouched, so CL dumps, posted G-code and goldens cannot move.
- Fails toward the enclosing (tilted) reading: downward, sideways, zero vector, NaN and inf are all "not upright"; the bound is `h <= tol*len` with `sin θ <= θ`, so no tilt above the tolerance is admitted.
- Threshold value and units: 1e-9 rad is ~4 orders under the finest commandable rotary step (0.001 deg = 1.7e-5 rad) and ~3 orders above the #938 noise (1e-10 deg = 1.7e-12 rad). Worst misplacement from judging a sub-tolerance tilt as upright is L*sin θ = 1e-6 mm for a 1 m stack, 1e-7 mm for a 100 mm holder disc, versus the 0.01 mm gouge tolerance. Tilt is judged per pose, so nothing accumulates.
- Both sides of the threshold are pinned: unit test `rounding_noise_is_upright_and_a_real_tilt_is_not` (1e-10 deg, 1e-12 components upright; 1.01x tolerance and 0.001 deg tilted; down/sideways/zero/NaN/inf refused) and `tilt_tolerance.rs` (1e-10 deg gives the same verdict as no pose; 1.01e-9 rad and 0.001 deg still convict the holder at both moves; law c2 fixture band also pinned both ways).
- All verify laws that branch on tilt were switched consistently (reach c/c3, c2/d2, posed steel, mesh steel, solid, posed contact, posed rapids, all-air); I found no remaining `is_vertical` branch in verify that was missed.
- Decision file `docs/decisions/938-tilt-tolerance.md` records the choice and the dropped options. No build.rs, scripts, `.github`, dependency, process-file, snapshot or CHANGELOG changes.

### Local results (trial-merged with upstream/main: already up to date, no conflicts)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` lib + 17 gate-mapped suites (incl. tilt_tolerance, posed_rapids, vertical_rapids, posed_fixture_midpose) | 18 binaries ok, 209 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion` real_tip, solid_law | ok, 9 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app` 10 gate-mapped suites (tool_body_bands, posed_contact, probe_reach, ...) | ok, 60 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

No existing fixture's verdict changed except the one noted below. Batch/release tiers and `--ignored` lanes were not run (as the PR states).

### Requested before merge
None blocking.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. The law (c) de-duplication (`reach.rs:201-206`, `warns.last() != Some(&hit)`) is a behaviour change beyond #938's title: an upright fat shank under a modelled body now reports one `ShankHit` instead of two (`tool_body_bands.rs:141-146` updated). The conviction itself is unchanged and a `part:false` beside a `part:true` hit is still kept, so I judge it safe; it is declared in the body and decision file. Anything counting warnings (reports/UI) would see one fewer line.
2. The tilted reading still has its cliff: a tilt just above 1e-9 rad (e.g. 1.01e-9) gives the false holder collision that #938 describes for noise. That is the conservative side and the decision file names the exact-dip alternative as a separate change.
3. Cosmetic: a double blank line before `#[cfg(test)]` at `upright.rs:51-52` (rustfmt would collapse it).
4. `avoid.rs`'s comment about being "as strict as the is_vertical the verifier branches on" is now slightly stale (noted in the decision file).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: ed277f7417467fbec0eca8aca4a58b4fdc2bad10 -->
**Independent review (maintainer side), high tier.** Verdict: **Needs changes before merge** - one small blocker. The fix itself is sound; the PR just has to take current `main`.

### What looks good
- One predicate, `verify::upright::is_upright`, one named constant (`UPRIGHT_TILT_RAD = 1e-9` rad), used by every verify law that branched on the exact `is_vertical`. `cl::is_vertical` stays exact, so CL, posted G-code and goldens cannot move. No `is_vertical` call is left in `crates/sim/src/verify/` outside `upright.rs`.
- The predicate fails closed. Downward, sideways, zero and non-finite axes read as tilted, and `h <= tol*len` bounds sin θ, so it never lets through a tilt above the tolerance.
- **The tolerance is safe, checked against numbers.** At 1e-9 rad, a 200 mm body above the tip moves at most 200 x 1e-9 = **2e-7 mm** sideways. A 50 mm holder rim dips at most 5e-8 mm. The laws' own margins are `gouge_tol` (0.01 mm, the kerf `r + gouge_tol`) and `z_tol` (1e-3 mm). So the worst error is about 5e4 times smaller than the tolerance it would have to hide behind, and judging such a pose as vertical cannot hide a collision larger than the laws' own tolerance. Even a 1 m stack gives 1e-6 mm.
- The `ShankHit` de-duplication is narrow. It drops only an *identical* `ShankHit{at, part}` that immediately follows another. A different move (`at`), a different `part`, or a different warning kind is never merged. Inside each group, a part hit still wins over a stock hit (`convicted` short-circuits on `Some(true)`).
- Tests live in `crates/sim/tests` with no app fixture. There is no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. Provenance lines are present. The decision file states the value, the reasoning and the dropped options.

### Local results (head ed277f74 trial-merged with main 3e9b8ae1, merge itself clean)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --tests` | **does not compile** as merged (below); with the one-line local fix, all suites pass, `tilt_tolerance` 5/5, lib 71/71 |
| app `tool_body_bands` | 13/13 (+ my scratch test, below) |
| app `tool_body_judged` / `sim_tool_body` / `verify` / `golden_cl` | 8/8 · 7/7 · 21/21 (2 ignored verdict-lane) · 25/25 |
| motion `solid_law` | 6/6 |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean (with the local fix) |

Scratch re-check of #843 / #938 (not committed), using the `beside_wall` fixture of `tool_body_bands.rs`:
- r4 and necked r3.5 shanks, tilted 30° toward the wall: `ShankHit{at:2, part:true}`. Tilted 30° away: no part hit. Vertical: clean. Tilted 1e-10°: the same as vertical.
- Holder r12 on a Ø8 cutter (#938): `None`, `[0,0,1]`, 1e-10° and exactly 1e-9 rad all give `[]`. 2e-9 rad and 0.01° give `ShankHit{at:2, part:true}` (the tilted reading).

So the #843 tilted path is unchanged above the tolerance, and #938 is fixed.

### Requested before merge
1. **`crates/sim/tests/tilt_tolerance.rs:82-97` does not compile against current `main`.** `main` gained `VerifyContext::model_excess` in #864 (PR #911, merged in 3e9b8ae1), so the struct literal in `judge_in` is now missing a field:
   ```
   error[E0063]: missing field `model_excess` in initializer of `VerifyContext<'_>`
   error: could not compile `camcraft-sim` (test "tilt_tolerance") due to 1 previous error
   ```
   Fix: `git merge origin/main` (no rebase or force-push), then add `model_excess: 0.0,` after `spindle: None,`. The other option is `..Default::default()`, the base #864 added for exactly this. Re-run `tilt_tolerance` after the change. GitHub shows the PR as mergeable because the conflict is semantic, not textual: merging as-is would break `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` on main.

### Notes (non-blocking)
- No other verdict changes: the only existing expectation that moved is `tool_body_bands::a_raised_foot_over_a_fat_shank_is_judged_stricter_than_the_cylinder` (duplicate -> one report). No goldens or snapshots changed.
- `reach.rs:203-206`: `warns.last()` is shared with the laws that run earlier, so (b2) `solid_hits` can push `ShankHit{at:i, part:true}` for the same move. If that is the last entry when (c) convicts move `i` with the same verdict, (c)'s copy is dropped as well. The value is identical, so nothing reachable is hidden. It is still a slightly wider merge than "per move and group"; a local `last` per move would keep it exact.
- The cliff stays. Just above the tolerance (2e-9 rad), the r12 holder flips to a part hit, because the tilted reading drops the band's bottom by its whole radius. This is the over-report the decision file names and leaves to a separate change. A follow-up issue for the exact R·sin θ enclosure would track it.
- `upright.rs:43-45`: two blank lines before `#[cfg(test)]` (rustfmt nit).
- `motion/.../avoid.rs`'s comment about "the is_vertical the verifier branches on" is now stale, as the decision file says. A one-line touch-up could go into the next motion PR.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 9b01def451ccdaea9ac006998608b1460dee5327 -->
**Re-review (maintainer side, high tier) of head 9b01def4.** Verdict: **Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The one blocker from the last review (ed277f74) is fixed, and both new commits hold up.

### What changed since ed277f74
- `62e1efda`, a merge of main with hand-resolved conflicts. I read its `git show --remerge-diff`:
  - `rapids_posed.rs` and `solid.rs` keep main's new `hits()` argument (`&[]` / `&axes_in(&fr, walls)`) together with the branch's `!is_upright`. Both sides are kept and nothing else moved.
  - `stock_top.rs` (main's #1091 site) swaps its own component test `a[0].abs() <= 1e-12 && a[1].abs() <= 1e-12 && a[2] > 0.0` for `is_upright`. The verifier now has one reader of "upright", and no ad-hoc test is left.
  - `tilt_tolerance.rs` takes `..Default::default()`, so it builds against `VerifyContext::model_excess`.
- `9b01def4`, which makes law (c) de-duplicate against its own per-move `reported` (`reach.rs:118-120, 213-218`) instead of `warns.last()`. This is exactly what the last review's note suggested: a `ShankHit` that (b2) pushed earlier can no longer swallow (c)'s report. It also pins #938 at the stock-top site and fixes the rustfmt nit.

### Earlier requests
1. **`tilt_tolerance.rs` did not compile against main (missing `model_excess`).** Fixed. It builds with current main merged in and passes 5/5.

### What looks good
- **One constant, one reader.** There is one constant, `UPRIGHT_TILT_RAD = 1e-9` rad (`upright.rs:25`), and one predicate, `is_upright`. Every verify law that branches on tilt calls it, including stock_top now: reach, sweep, laws (c2/d2), posed_steel, mesh_steel, solid, contact, rapids_posed, air and stock_top. `cl::is_vertical` stays exact, so CL dumps, posted G-code and goldens cannot move.
- **The tolerance hides no steel that matters.** Reading a tilt of 1e-9 rad as upright misplaces a 200 mm stack by 2e-7 mm sideways and dips a 15 mm rim by 1.5e-8 mm. That is about 5e4 times under `gouge_tol` and 5e3 times under `z_tol`. A post also rounds such a pose to A0/B0, so the upright reading is what the machine actually runs.
- **The edge is conservative on both sides.** Just inside the tolerance, the reading is the upright one, true to well under the margins above. Just outside it, the reading is the enclosing one: the band bottom drops by its whole radius and the disc widens. I found no pose where neither reading covers the stack.

### Local results (head 9b01def4 trial-merged with main 890de463, clean)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-sim` lib | 96/96 |
| sim `tilt_tolerance` / `posed_rapids` / `posed_fixture_midpose` / `vertical_rapids` / `sideways_rapids` / `radial_rapids` / `midmove_pose` / `fixture_mesh_posed` / `fixture_stack_span` / `model_excess` / `overhang_laws` / `prior_columns` | 5 / 5 / 3 / 16 / 3 / 15 / 5 / 9 (+1 ignored) / 8 / 5 / 13 / 2, all pass |
| app `tool_body_bands` / `tool_body` / `tool_body_judged` / `tool_body_drill_probe` / `posed_contact` / `probe_reach` / `tilt` / `rotary_verify` / `rotary_fixtures` / `self_centering_vise_tilted` / `fixture_mesh_posed` / `c_axis_fixture` / `solid_law` / `verify` / `vertical_rapid_stock` / `stepped_stock_rapid` / `stepped_stock_link` | 13 / 12 / 8 / 5 / 5 / 5 / 8 / 9 / 4 / 3 / 2 / 2 / 4 / 21 (+2 ignored) / 10 / 8 / 3, all pass |
| motion `real_tip` / `solid_law` | 3 / 6 |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Throwaway probes** (local only, removed before clippy). Tilts tried: 0, 1e-12, 5e-10, 0.999e-9, exactly 1e-9, 1.0000001e-9 and 2e-9 rad, each toward +X, -X, +Y and -Y.
- **reach (c), wide-holder fixture:** clean up to and including 1e-9, two `ShankHit`s from 1.0000001e-9. The tight-pocket fat shank (convicted when upright) is convicted at every tilt.
- **c2 fixture band:** a clamp under the holder is clear up to 1e-9 and hit just above it. A clamp the holder touches is hit at every tilt.
- **mid-turn sweep (c3), upright turning to +X:** clean up to 1e-9, `ShankHit` above it.
- **posed rapids and solid, `posed_rapids` ledge:** a rapid through the ledge and a feed into it are convicted at every tilt. The under-ledge rapid keeps `RapidInStock` on both sides, so its verdict does not flip at the edge.
- **stock_top (#1091) dive at Z 22:** acquitted up to 1e-9, convicted above it. The deep dive at Z 5 is convicted at every tilt.
- **`is_upright` edge cases:**
  - Exactly `[1e-9, 0, 1]` is upright, and so is 0.999x. 1.000001x is not.
  - Diagonal 0.7x/0.7x is upright; 0.71x/0.71x is not.
  - Scaled axes (1e±300, subnormal) read the same angle. `1e308` in every component (where `hypot` overflows) is not upright.
  - NaN, zero vector, downward axis and `[1e-12, 0, inf]` are not upright. `-0.0` is upright.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **Comment wording, `upright.rs:40-41`.** The comment says "θ ≥ sin θ, so `h <= tol·len` admits no tilt above the tolerance". The inequality runs the other way: the test bounds sin θ, so it admits θ up to asin(1e-9), which is 1e-9 + ~1.7e-28 rad. That makes no difference in practice. Suggested wording: "admits sin θ ≤ tol".
2. **The decision file (`docs/decisions/938-tilt-tolerance.md`) does not list the stock-top site.** That site moved from a ~1e-12 component test to 1e-9 rad, and it is an acquittal path. The numbers above cover it, and `a_rounding_noise_pose_is_an_upright_dive_and_a_real_tilt_is_not` pins it. It would be worth one line in the law list.
3. **Pre-existing, not from this PR (same reading on main, where `is_vertical` is also false).**
   - An axis with an infinite component, e.g. `[1e-12, 0, inf]`, takes the tilted branch, and reach (c) then convicts nothing. Even the tight-pocket shank that is convicted when upright passes clean. The NonFinite law (`engine.rs:32-36`) checks only `from` and `to`, not `axis`.
   - Reach also reads a non-unit axis's `a[2]` as-is (`reach.rs:139-142`). A 7x-scaled 2e-9 tilt loses its `ShankHit` and keeps only the sweep's `SweepHit`.

   Both are worth a follow-up (degenerate pose: refuse, or normalize first). Neither is made worse here.
4. `avoid.rs`'s comment about "the is_vertical the verifier branches on" is still stale, as the decision file says.
5. **Stacked PR.** #1306 is stacked on exactly this head (9b01def4). This head is a sound base for it and does not depend on it to be safe: the tilted reading here is the whole-radius over-reach, which is the conservative side, and #1306 only narrows it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
